name: Pixilation
visualIdentity: Live performers are photographed frame by frame in deliberate poses, with scene and costume continuity. Sliding, sudden position changes, and object interaction use readable direction and held exposures. Pixilation is distinct from pixel art and ordinary low-frame-rate footage.
suitableUses: Explicit fit: surreal performance, music videos, energetic social campaigns, and campaigns or event promos with stepping typography. More generally suitable for video or image-sequence HTML when discrete photographed poses serve the idea; that HTML suitability is inferred.
limitations: Requires planned and photographed human poses; lowering a continuous video's frame rate is not authentic pixilation. No intrinsic palette or dedicated renderer is specified. Preserve costume, lighting, and scene continuity. Avoid beat flashing, smooth tweens over stepped footage, face-obscuring type, and indiscriminate spring motion.
palette: No canonical style palette is specified. Keep performers, environments, lighting, and source artwork unchanged. Optional suggestions for new presentation elements only: background #EEE7DC, foreground #343C43, accent #8A9288; use discrete colors, no gradients. Accent with foreground text has 3.495 contrast and is unsuitable for body text; the suggested foreground/background pair has 9.127, but verify actual compositing. Task, brand, or reference colors take precedence.
motionAndInteraction: Plan pose order and exposure holds; make jumps and trajectories legible without automatically interpolating poses. Pose exposure rate may differ from delivery frame rate. For video, derive deterministic states from seekable composition time; for interactive HTML, an image-sequence player can sync to an event table with pause and reduced-motion stills. Backward and direct seeks should resolve coherently.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voice, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; pose jumps may align to a verified beat table. Honor supplied choices and assets, and check intelligibility, balance, clipping, and sync.
assetRequirements: Prepare photographed performer frames or layers with preserved alpha where needed, consistent dimensions, clear numbering, and a layer manifest. Keep costume, scene, and lighting continuous. Inspect assets before assembly. Python may preprocess sequences; FFmpeg can encode frames and combine audio. Tools are suggestions, not claims about source production.
combinations: Suggested music hybrid: style-105 timing aligns exposure holds and position jumps to verified beats while preserving readable travel direction and continuity. Suggested typography hybrid: style-093 type steps on the photo cadence, uses #343C43 with #8A9288 accents, sits in negative space, and holds for reading. Avoid smooth type tweens and covering faces. Other combinations are unspecified.
productionApproach: Photograph and organize poses first; select visual and motion methods for fidelity and assets. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, and record why. Keep rendering and motion logic in their own layers; use one owner per animated property. Inspect key frames and the full rendered video. Interactive scroll or pointer behavior belongs only to HTML delivery.
